spawnBayes

spawnBayes estimates salmon spawner abundance and run timing from repeated live-count surveys. Unlike traditional area-under-the-curve approaches,spawnBayes` estimates abundance, run timing, and their associated uncertainty while allowing residence time to vary among years.

The package is designed to support salmon stock assessment and escapement monitoring programs. Users provide survey dates and spawner counts and obtain estimates of annual abundance, run timing, effective residence time, and associated uncertainty.

Documentation

Online documentation, reference manuals, and a complete worked example are available at:

spawnBayes documentation

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("SiRE-P/spawnBayes")

Prerequisites

spawnBayes uses cmdstanr and requires a local installation of CmdStan.

Install cmdstanr:

install.packages(
  "cmdstanr",
  repos = c(
    "https://mc-stan.org/r-packages/",
    getOption("repos")
  )
)

Then follow the official CmdStan installation guide:

https://mc-stan.org/docs/cmdstan-guide/installation.html

Verify the installation:

cmdstanr::cmdstan_version()

Data Requirements

Required columns:

Variable Description
date Survey date
spawner_counts Number of live spawners observed

Optional columns:

Variable Description
observer_efficiency Proportion of fish detected during a survey (0-1)
coverage Proportion of spawning habitat surveyed (0-1)

If observer_efficiency or coverage are omitted, values of 1 are assumed.

Quick Example 

library(spawnBayes)

data(clemens_sockeye)

fit <- fit_spawner(
  clemens_sockeye,
  assumed_residence = 15.5
)

plot_run_curve(fit)

Estimate annual abundance:

abundance(fit)

Estimate run timing:

timing(fit)

Worked Example

A complete worked example using Clemens Creek Sockeye salmon data is available in the documentation:

Clemens Creek Sockeye Example

Data Template

Create a template CSV file in the current working directory:

template_file()

This creates:

spawnBayes_template.csv

containing the required and optional input columns.
